title: Assured Throughput Commitment Wording and Escalation Lexicon
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Purpose: Draft a customer-facing set of commitment statements, objective measurement definitions, error-budget calculation, and contractual remediation lexicon for Dedicated capacity offerings. This ticket consolidates PM rationale, the preferred metric names, engineering instrumentation requirements, proposed credit formulas, and an escalation/playbook vocabulary for sales/legal use.

Background: Customers buying Dedicated commit to reserved GPU pools and expect predictable throughput. Existing contracts reference 'throughput SLAs' and credits in vague terms. We need clear, measurable commitments that map to telemetry and automated crediting while preserving operational flexibility (autoscale/fallback) to avoid false positives.

Primary deliverables:
- Finalized set of SLA term definitions using unique metric names that map to implementation (see "Telemetry mapping" below).
- Error budget formula and example computations for monthly billing windows.
- Credit matrix and payout cadence (pro-rata credit basis, caps).
- Required instrumentation and dashboard queries for SLO measurement.
- Plain-language remediation lexicon for contracts and support playbooks (notice windows, acceptable maintenance, emergency thresholds).
- Escalation steps for customers, and internal on-call/runbook triggers.

Metric definitions (proposed, novel naming to reduce ambiguity):
- Guaranteed Sustained Token Throughput (GSTT): median tokens/second per committed GPU averaged over rolling 60-minute windows, evaluated hourly.
- Peak Guaranteed Concurrency (PGC): 99th-percentile concurrent active streams per node over a 24-hour rolling window.
- Throughput Degradation Event (TDE): any continuous 15-minute interval where GSTT falls below 90% of the committed GSTT for that customer's capacity band. Multiple contiguous TDEs are coalesced for crediting logic.

Error budget and credit formula (example):
- Monthly committed GSTT = C (tokens/sec/node). Observed delivered GSTT = D (tokens/sec/node) computed as 95th percentile of hourly medians during the billing month.
- Shortfall S = max(0, C - D). Error budget utilization = S / C.
- Credit tiering (proposed):
  - <5% shortfall: no credit (operational tolerance).
  - 5%–15% shortfall: 10% monthly service credit prorated to the committed capacity impacted.
  - 15%–40% shortfall: 30% monthly service credit prorated.
  - >40% shortfall: 60% monthly service credit plus 30-day remediation plan requirement.
- Credits apply to monthly platform fees for Dedicated; usage overage and burst allowances are billed separately and not eligible for credit unless impacted by capacity shortfall.

Notice and remediation language (plain-language):
- Notice window: Redwood will notify customers within 60 minutes of detecting a TDE that persists > 30 minutes.
- Investigation and short-term remediation window: Redwood will provide a preliminary incident report and mitigation ETA within 4 business hours.
- Customer credit request: automatically computed and applied in the next billing cycle; customers may request manual review within 14 days with evidence.

Autoscale and fleet control interplay (to be reflected in contract text):
- Reserved pool behavior: Dedicated pools include a configurable warm pool for burst. Contracted GSTT assumes warm-pool enabled where customers purchased burst add-on. If warm-pool is disabled via customer choice, GSTT commitments are reduced proportionally and documented.
- Failure-safe fallback: for transient, system-wide shortages, requests will be routed to best-effort hosted variants if policy permits; such fallbacks do not count toward GSTT delivered for Dedicated. Contracts will include an explicit failure-mode carve-out describing automatic routing and notice obligations.
- Autoscale triggers: the platform will maintain X% headroom by default (engineering to propose exact value). Autoscale cooldown and canary policies will be described in the technical appendix; customer-visible commitment refers only to delivered GSTT after autoscale stabilization (i.e., after up to 10 minutes of scaling).

Telemetry mapping and instrumentation asks (engineering):
- Expose a per-customer timeseries: dedicated.gstt.hourly_median and dedicated.pgc.24h_p99.
- Export TDE windows as dedicated.tde.events with start/end tags and cause categorization (hardware/infra/placement/autoscale).
- Dashboard: single-pane SLO dashboard and an SLO-exportable CSV endpoint for legal/finance reconciliation.
- PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/2128 (work in progress).

Tradeoffs and open questions:
- Strictness vs. operability: tighter definitions reduce dispute but increase exposure and potential payouts; recommended leaning toward conservative thresholds combined with remediation obligations.
- Measurement window selection: hourly medians reduce noise from microbursts but might mask repeated short outages; we propose a hybrid (hourly medians + 15-min TDE detection) to capture both.
- Credit caps: need alignment with finance on maximum monthly liability per account.

Review feedback summary (so far):
- Legal (S. Morgan): prefers phrase "Guaranteed Sustained Token Throughput" over colloquial "throughput SLA" and requests a carve-out for scheduled maintenance >= 72 hours notice.
- Engineering (L. Choi): asks for explicit labeling of telemetry metrics and a determinism section for aggregation to avoid off-by-one counting differences.
- Sales (R. Kapoor): requests a simplified two-line customer summary for the quote process and a short FAQ to reduce negotiation friction.

Next steps:
- Incorporate legal edits and finalize contract paragraph examples by 2025-02-26.
- Engineering to land telemetry PR and dashboard by 2025-03-04.
- Draft customer-facing FAQ and example contract snippets for the pricing team by 2025-03-07.

Relevant artifacts: Confluence draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/DED/Throughput+Commitments, GH PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/2128, Early SLO dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/throughput-slos
